# 7416 - Hex inverter buffer/driver with open-collector high-voltage output

Package DIP-14 · family 74 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/7416.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/7416.json)

## Symbol

| As printed in ND-13.003.01, page 7 | Drawn in ND style | Drawn in modern style |
|---|---|---|
| ![7416 as printed in the 1976 symbol manual](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/7416.png) | ![7416 drawn in nd style](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/shapes/not-buf-ochv-bar1.png) | ![7416 drawn in modern style](../../../catalog/symbols/modern/shapes/not-buf-ochv-bar1.png) |

A box with a pointed right end and one vertical bar about a third of the way in from the left edge. High-voltage open collector: works like a plain open collector (it can only pull the line low; a pull-up resistor makes the 1, and several outputs may share one line), but the output transistor stands a higher voltage and a larger current. Per the TI datasheets: 7406/7407 up to 30 V, 7416/7417 up to 15 V, and up to 40 mA pulled low; a plain open collector such as 7405 stands only 5.5 V and 16 mA, so its pull-up must go to +5 V. High-voltage parts can switch a lamp, a relay or a 12 V line directly. The logic is the same. In the modern drawing it is marked HV beside the open-collector mark; that label is ours, not a standard symbol.

How to tell it on a drawing: Bar inside the pointed box = open collector, inverting driver (high voltage). Compare 7406 (diagonal instead of bar).

All symbols: [symbol catalogue](../../SYMBOL-CATALOG.md).

## Functions

| Output pin | Formula | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1Y = NOT 1A | 1Y is the inverse of 1A. Open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up. |
| 4 | 2Y = NOT 2A | 2Y is the inverse of 2A. Open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up. |
| 6 | 3Y = NOT 3A | 3Y is the inverse of 3A. Open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up. |
| 8 | 4Y = NOT 4A | 4Y is the inverse of 4A. Open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up. |
| 10 | 5Y = NOT 5A | 5Y is the inverse of 5A. Open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up. |
| 12 | 6Y = NOT 6A | 6Y is the inverse of 6A. Open collector: the high level needs an outside pull-up. |

## Electrical

| Value | Figure |
|---|---|
| outputLowMaxCurrentMa | 40 |
| outputMaxVoltageV | 15 |
| inputSchmitt | no |
| notes | Buffer/driver: IOL 40 mA vs 16 mA for 7404, so it sinks two and a half times as much; the output may be pulled up to 15 V (7406: 30 V). Off-state leakage max 0.25 mA at VOH 15 V. |

## Propagation delays

All measured at VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, RL 110 ohm, CL 15 pF.

| From | To | Edge | Typ ns | Max ns |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| any | Y | PLH | 10 | 15 |
| any | Y | PHL | 15 | 23 |

## Notes

The datasheet gives no minimum propagation delay; minNs is null (the path-delay function uses 0 ns). No setup/hold/pulse-width limits apply to a gate, so timingLimits is empty.

## Sources

- [TI SN5406/SN5416/SN7406/SN7416 datasheet SDLS031A](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn7416.pdf) - 1, 3; SN7416
